# origin observability commands

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen_cli_reference.py from `origin --help` of the release scripts/origin-cli.version pins (v1.18.0).
     Do not edit by hand: fix the help text in origincloudhq/cli, or scripts/cli_reference_overrides.yml, and rerun. -->

This page lists every `origin observability` command. For the options every `origin` command accepts, see [Global options](../../platform/reference/cli.md#global-options); for what each metric counts, see [Metrics reference](metrics.md).

## origin observability

The metrics the platform collects for a project's compute instances, volumes and network interfaces: CPU time, network traffic, and volume reads and writes. Every metric is a counter, a running total that grows while the instance runs. A query never returns the raw total: for each period of the window it asks for, it returns the counter's average per-second increase over the period (`RATE`) or its total increase (`INCREASE`). The platform collects a value for each counter every 30 seconds while the instance runs, and keeps the values for 90 days. A volume or a network interface is measured through the instance it is attached to, so it has values only while attached to a running instance.

Every `origin observability` command also accepts:

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--endpoint <URL>` | Base URL to send the calls to, such as a test server's, instead of the service's own host: `https://observability.origincloudapis.eu`, or `https://observability.{region}.origincloudapis.eu` when the profile names a `region`. It must be `https://`, or `http://` to this machine (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `[::1]`). Environment variable: `ORIGINCLOUD_OBSERVABILITY_ENDPOINT`. |

### query-time-series

Returns a resource's time series for the metrics asked, one per metric, in the order asked. Needs `observability.metric.get` on the resource. A query is limited in what it costs. Its points, the window's length divided by `--period`, plus one, for each of its metrics, are at most 11,000 in all, and an organization may run 60 queries a minute and 4 at a time. A query over any of these limits is refused with `FAILED_PRECONDITION`, the same message for all three: one within the points limit succeeds when sent again a few seconds later. Each query answered is billed as one request, however many series or points it returns; a refused one isn't.

```sh
origin observability query-time-series [OPTIONS] --parent <PROJECT> --resource <RESOURCE> --metric <METRIC> --start-time <TIME> --end-time <TIME> --period <DURATION> --statistic <STATISTIC>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--parent <PROJECT>` | yes | The project the resource is in, `projects/{project}`. Its id, or its whole name, `projects/{project}`. |
| `--resource <RESOURCE>` | yes | The resource whose metrics to return, in `parent`: an instance, `projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/instances/{instance}`, a volume, `projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/volumes/{volume}`, or a network interface, `projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/networkInterfaces/{network_interface}`. |
| `--metric <METRIC>` | yes | The metrics to return, such as `oc_compute_instance_cpu_seconds_total`, at least one. A metric of another kind of resource returns a series without points. Repeat for more. |
| `--start-time <TIME>` | yes | The start of the window: the first point is at it. As RFC 3339, such as `2026-11-01T12:00:00Z`. |
| `--end-time <TIME>` | yes | The end of the window, not before `--start-time`. As RFC 3339, such as `2026-11-01T12:00:00Z`. |
| `--period <DURATION>` | yes | The length of each period, in whole seconds, at least one: the points are this far apart, and each covers the period that ends at it. A value is collected every 30 seconds and a point needs two inside its period, so a period under 60 seconds often has none. Such as `30s` or `1m`. |
| `--statistic <STATISTIC>` | yes | How each point is computed. Possible values: `RATE`, `INCREASE`. |
